spec.title: SLA clock for every complaint case
spec.goal: Operators cannot see which complaints are about to breach their response deadline. Add an SLA clock: the backend computes, for every complaint, sla_due_at from its received/created date and its severity or priority (critical 1 day, high 3 days, medium 7 days, low 15 days; treat unknown as medium), and sla_status: 'breached' when now is past the due time, 'at_risk' within the last 20% of the window, else 'on_track'. Expose sla_due_at and sla_status on the complaint list and detail APIs. In the frontend Cases workspace (and the Complaints list if it shows the same records), show an SLA badge per case with a clear label and color, and add a filter to show only cases that are at risk or breached. Add backend unit tests for the SLA computation (including boundary cases) and an API test, plus a frontend test for the badge.
spec.constraints: Compute SLA in one backend function; do not duplicate the rules in the frontend. Keep existing API fields unchanged (only add). All checks must pass.

tasks.title: Implement single SLA computation function with severity windows and status thresholds
acceptance: A single exported function in the backend computes sla_due_at from the complaint's received/created date plus severity window: critical 1 day, high 3 days, medium 7 days, low 15 days, and falls back to medium for missing or unknown severity.

The same function returns sla_status: 'breached' when now is strictly after sla_due_at, 'at_risk' when now is within the last 20% of the window (including the exact 20% boundary), otherwise 'on_track'.
SLA rules are defined in exactly one place in the backend with no duplicated thresholds elsewhere in backend or frontend.
Existing complaint-related fields and values are unchanged.

tasks.title: Expose sla_due_at and sla_status on complaint list and detail APIs additively
acceptance: GET /api/complaints returns sla_due_at and sla_status for every item.
GET /api/complaints/{complaint_id} returns sla_due_at and sla_status.
All previously returned fields remain present with unchanged names and semantics; only new fields are added.
The API layer calls the single SLA function rather than re-deriving rules.

tasks.title: Backend unit tests for SLA computation incl. boundary cases and an API test
acceptance: Unit tests cover each severity window (critical/high/medium/low) and the unknown-severity fallback to medium.
Boundary cases covered: now exactly at sla_due_at is not breached, now just past due is breached, now exactly at the 20% at_risk threshold is at_risk, and just before it is on_track.
An API test asserts sla_due_at and sla_status are present on the complaint list and detail responses and that pre-existing fields are unchanged.
All new tests pass under the repository's backend test command.

tasks.title: SLA badge component and rendering in Cases workspace and Complaints list
acceptance: A reusable SLA badge renders a clear text label (On track / At risk / Breached) with distinct colors per status and shows the due date/time.
Badge is shown per case in the Cases workspace and in the Complaints list for the same records.
Missing or unrecognized sla_status renders a neutral fallback without crashing.
Frontend does not compute SLA thresholds; it only reads sla_due_at and sla_status from the API.

tasks.title: At-risk/breached filter in Cases workspace and Complaints list
acceptance: A filter control shows only cases whose sla_status is 'at_risk' or 'breached', with the active state visible.
Clearing the filter restores the unfiltered list without data loss or refetch errors.
Filtering relies solely on the API-provided sla_status field.
Existing filters and list behavior are unaffected when the SLA filter is off.

tasks.title: Frontend test for SLA badge rendering and risk filter
acceptance: Test asserts the badge renders the correct label and color class for on_track, at_risk, and breached, plus the neutral fallback for missing status.
Test asserts the at-risk/breached filter shows only matching cases and clearing it restores all cases.
Test passes under the repository's frontend test command.

tasks.title: Document SLA rules and new API fields
acceptance: docs/testing.md or docs/architecture.md documents the severity windows, the 20% at-risk rule, and the additive sla_due_at/sla_status fields.
Documentation stays consistent with the implemented behavior and does not duplicate thresholds as an alternative source of truth.
